prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added `heading_offset` (a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0) to `markdown.Markdown` and `markdown.markdown`, plus `--heading-offset N` on the command line. The full test suite passes: 1143 tests, 112 skipped. Any other value, including floats, strings, booleans and None, raises ValueError; on the command line that shows up as a Python traceback. The shift is done by a new step in `markdown/treeprocessors.py` that runs after headings are built and before `toc`, so `toc` sees the shifted levels in its tokens and `toc_depth`. It covers hash and underline headings and every heading `md_in_html` puts in the document. That includes a raw `<h3 markdown="1">`, which I chose to shift. Plain raw HTML headings without `markdown="1"` are left unchanged. `toc`'s `baselevel` is applied on top of the offset. The docs (`library.md`, `cli.md`, `toc.md`) and the changelog are updated. flake8 and pyflakes are not installed here, so lint was not run.
